text.p: Danish shipping, oil and gas heavyweight A.P. Moeller on Wednesday upheld earlier forecasts of a better full year 1997 result than 1996.

"There is nothing more to add to our annual report forecasts for 1997. Our overall shipping activities result for the whole year looks like being better than in 1996," board chairman Maersk Mc-Kinney Moeller told the group's annual general meeting.

He added that supply vessel operations got off to a particularly good start in 1997, while the market for crude oil and refined products had tailed off somewhat and gas tanker earnings remained disappointing.
Moeller earned a net two billion crowns in 1996 from its core shipping activities, up from 1.59 billion crowns in 1995, the group announced in its annual report last April.
